facts.fact: The page states that linear TV still accounts for nearly 90% of television viewing time across 86 countries, without naming a source for the figure.
facts.quote: it still accounts for nearly **90% of television viewing time** across 86 countries.

facts.fact: The page states that linear TV captures nearly 90% of all ad-watching time on TV screens, attributing this to its higher ad load than most streaming services.
facts.unit: % of ad-watching time on TV screens
facts.quote: It captures nearly **90% of all ad-watching time** on TV screens, simply because it has a higher ad load than most streaming services.

facts.fact: According to scale-marketing.com's 2025 media trends report as cited by the page, US linear TV viewing is projected to settle at 56.5% of total video time.
facts.quote: Even as US linear TV viewing is projected to settle at **56.5% of total video time**, it remains the heavyweight champion.

facts.fact: Adwave states that its small-business ads can run on major linear channels such as NBC and ESPN while being shown only to chosen neighborhoods and customer types.
facts.quote: Your ad can run on major channels like NBC and ESPN, but only be shown to the specific neighborhoods and customer types you want to reach.

facts.fact: Adwave describes itself as combining ad creation and media buying so small businesses can prepare campaigns for TV, search, and social.
facts.quote: Adwave combines ad creation and media buying so small businesses can prepare campaigns for TV, search, and social.

facts.fact: Adwave says a campaign can be put on the air with a budget as small as $50.
facts.quote: You can get a campaign on the air with a budget as small as **$50**, which gives you total control over your spending.

facts.fact: The page says TV advertising was historically something only big brands with six-figure budgets could consider.
facts.quote: something only big brands with six-figure budgets could even think about

facts.fact: Per the page, Reach is the total number of unique households that see an ad at least once.
facts.quote: This is simply the total number of unique households that see your ad at least once.

facts.fact: Per the page, Frequency is the average number of times a single household sees an ad over the course of a campaign.
facts.quote: This tells you the average number of times a single household sees your ad over the course of the campaign.

facts.fact: Per the page, Impressions equal Reach multiplied by Frequency.
facts.quote: It's just your Reach multiplied by your Frequency.

facts.fact: Per the page, CPM (Cost Per Mille) means cost per thousand impressions.
facts.quote: This is a fancy way of saying "Cost Per Thousand" impressions.

facts.fact: Per the page, GRPs are calculated by multiplying Reach (as a percentage of the total market) by average Frequency.
facts.quote: **GRPs** are calculated by multiplying your Reach (as a percentage of the total market) by your average Frequency.

facts.fact: In the page's illustrative example, a campaign with 100 GRPs could mean reaching 50% of the market an average of two times.
facts.quote: a campaign with **100 GRPs** could mean you reached **50%** of the market an average of two times

facts.fact: In the page's illustrative example, 10,000 households each seeing an ad three times yields 30,000 impressions.
facts.quote: **10,000 households x 3 views = 30,000 impressions**.

facts.fact: Adwave states that ads can be placed on NBC, ESPN, and Hulu.
facts.quote: You can get your ad on huge channels like **NBC**, **ESPN**, and **Hulu**

facts.fact: Adwave states that its hyper-local targeting can limit ads to specific zip codes or neighborhoods.
facts.quote: you can set it to _only_ show up in the specific neighborhoods or zip codes where your best customers live.

facts.fact: The page names home services, healthcare, real estate, and retail as industries for which linear TV via Adwave is a useful option.
facts.value: home services, healthcare, real estate, retail
facts.quote: This is a useful option for local businesses in home services, healthcare, real estate, and retail.

facts.fact: Adwave says local TV campaigns can start as low as $50.
facts.quote: With campaigns starting as low as **$50**, this isn't just for the big players anymore.

facts.fact: Adwave says a targeted local campaign on major channels can start at $30 per day.
facts.quote: you can get a targeted local campaign up and running on major channels for as little as **$30/day**.

facts.fact: Adwave says users can target specific neighborhoods or zip codes when placing a TV ad.
facts.quote: You can zero in on specific neighborhoods or zip codes, making sure your message only lands in front of people who can become customers.

facts.fact: Adwave states its dashboard lets advertisers track impressions and reach in real time after an ad goes live.
facts.quote: you can watch its performance unfold on a real-time dashboard.

facts.fact: The page states that a commercial created in the Adwave platform is produced with modern tools, but it gives no cost or time figure for production.
facts.quote: Modern tools handle all the heavy lifting, turning your ideas into a polished, broadcast-ready ad that makes your brand look great.
